name: Gulab Jamun
description: Soft golden milk-powder dumplings fried gently and soaked in warm cardamom sugar syrup.
ingredients: ¼ cup milk, approximately and added gradually
Neutral oil or ghee for frying
method: Combine sugar, water and cardamom in a saucepan. Simmer for 6–8 minutes until the sugar dissolves and a light syrup forms. Add lemon juice if using, then keep the syrup warm rather than boiling hard.
Mix milk powder, flour and baking powder. Rub in 2 tbsp ghee, then add milk a little at a time to form a soft dough. Do not over-knead.
Rest the dough for 5–10 minutes, then shape into small smooth balls without cracks; they will expand while soaking.
Heat frying oil or ghee over low to medium-low heat. Fry the balls slowly, moving them gently for even colour, until deep golden and cooked through.
Let the fried balls rest briefly, then place them in warm—not vigorously boiling—syrup.
Soak for at least 1–2 hours so the gulab jamun absorb syrup and soften before serving.
tips: High frying heat can brown the outside before the centre cooks.
Add milk gradually because milk-powder mixtures can become sticky quickly.
Smooth, crack-free balls are less likely to split while frying.
storage: Refrigerate covered in syrup for up to 3 days. Warm gently before serving if desired.
